summary.text: An 18-year-old male presented in December 2022 with intermittent fever, nasal congestion and bloody nasal discharge that had persisted for four years, after earlier sinus surgery for sinusitis and surgery for secretory otitis media. Examination showed no lymph node enlargement, jaundice, rash or petechiae, and he had no underlying diseases or family history of similar or genetic disease.

Nasal endoscopy and MRI showed nasopharyngeal lymphoid hyperplasia and soft tissue thickening, whole blood EBV DNA was positive, and PET/CT showed mucosal thickening with concentrated radioactivity. Nasopharyngeal biopsy indicated EBV-associated T-lymphocyte proliferative disease, grade I, and systemic CAEBV was diagnosed from history and examination results.

He received tislelizumab from January 2023 with persistent intermittent fever, and a second biopsy in February 2023 showed progression to grade II; the DDGP regimen was recommended, and after 3 cycles of chemotherapy high fever persisted. Pancytopenia and bone marrow hemophagocytic macrophages led to an HLH diagnosis treated with etoposide and dexamethasone. Allo-HSCT was advised but not performed, and he had a nucleocyte collection, low-dose CHOP bridging chemotherapy and CAR-T cell infusion.

After CAR-T infusion his temperature normalized and EBV DNA dropped below normal, and he was discharged. Three months later left lower limb pain developed and pathology still showed EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disease; radiotherapy relieved the pain and oral etoposide maintenance was given. He was monitored for 17 months without recurrence, with undetectable whole blood EBV DNA.

Nasal endoscopy showed inferior turbinate swelling, MRI showed no significant nasopharyngeal soft tissue thickening, and PET/CT showed slight nasopharyngeal and nasal cavity thickening with concentrated radiation distribution. Multiple biopsies indicated EBV-associated T/NK-lymphocyte proliferative disease of at least grade 2 with positive EBER and monoclonal TCR rearrangement, and systemic CAEBV was diagnosed.

She received DDGP chemotherapy with intermittent high fevers, and disease progression was found after four cycles in June 2024. Pancytopenia, bone marrow hemophagocytic cells and blood mNGS findings led to an HLH diagnosis treated with etoposide and dexamethasone, and in July 2024 the regimen was changed to sidabenamide and lenalidomide while her condition continued to deteriorate.

After hematology consultation allo-HSCT was recommended, but for financial reasons it was not performed until three months after progression to HLH, following whole body irradiation, cyclophosphamide and thiotepa. After transplantation she developed persistent high fever, severe anemia, worsening organ function and a carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli blood culture, and died in October 2024 of multiple organ failure and septic shock.
